choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) anticipate (B) restricted (C) suffer 근거 ❶❷❹❺ 해설: (A) ❶❷ 손이 의식보다 먼저 앎 → anticipate (precede도 성립, imitate·repeat·interrupt는 오류) / (B) ❹ prevented from gesturing → restricted (blocked도 성립, encouraged·exaggerated·recorded는 반대) / (C) ❺ deleterious effects → suffer (decline·deteriorate도 성립, improve·recover는 반대). 요약문 해석: 실수를 고치려고 말을 멈추기 직전에 손짓을 멈추므로, 손짓은 말을 뒤따르기보다 말을 (A) 앞질러 내다보는 것 같다. 손짓이 (B) 제한되면 말은 머뭇거리게 되고 기억, 문제 해결, 설명이 모두 (C) 타격을 입는다.
choice.psg: ❶ When we realize we’ve said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. ❷ Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands “know” what we’re going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. ❸ Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. ❹ When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. ❺ Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. ❻ Far from tagging along as speech’s clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
choice.body: Because we stop gesturing just before we stop speaking to fix an error, gesture seems to (A)________ our words rather than follow them; when it is (B)________, speech grows hesitant and memory, problem solving, and explanation all (C)________.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: Gestures prepare the mind in advance so the right word is ready when we need it.
Listeners use a speaker’s gestures to guess which word will come next in the sentence.
Gestures literally draw the shapes of written words in the air for listeners to read.
Gestures distract the mind and make it harder for speakers to find the right word quickly.
Gestures are used mainly to make speakers look more confident in front of an audience.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) perceive (B) conscious (C) hallucinate 근거 ❷❸❹❻❼ 해설: (A) ❷❸ not designed to sense on its own → perceive (detect도 성립, store·imagine·forget은 오류) / (B) ❹ kept awake during brain surgery → conscious (awake·alert도 성립, sleeping·unhealthy는 오류) / (C) ❼ hallucinations → hallucinate (malfunction도 성립, relax·recover·concentrate는 반대). 요약문 해석: 뇌는 스스로는 아무것도 (A) 지각할 수 없고 전적으로 감각에 의존하는데, 이것이 (B) 의식이 있는 환자에게 수술을 진행할 수 있는 이유와, 외부 입력이 차단된 사람들이 곧 (C) 환각을 보기 시작하는 이유를 설명해 준다.
choice.psg: ❶ Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. ❷ Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. ❸ For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. ❹ In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. ❺ The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, “Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses.” ❻ This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. ❼ They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. ❽ From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.
choice.body: The brain cannot (A)________ anything by itself; it relies wholly on the senses, which explains why surgery can proceed on (B)________ patients and why people cut off from outside input soon begin to (C)________.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

lack of feeling in an exposed brain
ancient recognition of the brain’s limits
exclusive role of the sense organs

Surgeons keep themselves awake for long hours by talking constantly with the nurses standing nearby.
Patients must stay awake because the brain becomes extremely sensitive to pain during the surgery itself.

choice.body: For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, “Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses.”

choice.ex: (A) strain (B) loosen (C) matters 근거 ❶❹❺❻❼ 해설: (A) ❹ tension → strain (stress도 성립, heat·light·sound는 오류) / (B) ❺❻ 늘리는 힘이 훨씬 커서 마찰이 먼저 극복됨 → loosen (slip·detach 도 성립, shrink·melt는 오류) / (C) ❼ the friction with which we need to concern ourselves → matters (counts도 성립, fails·disappears·changes는 오류). 요약문 해석: 박힌 못은 마찰 때문에 제자리에 있으며, 결합된 블록을 떼어 내면 못 안에 (A) 긴장(응력)도 생기지만, 못은 부러지기보다 (B) 헐거워질 가능 성이 훨씬 크므로, 마찰이 진정으로 (C) 중요한 요인이다.
choice.psg: ❶ Once a nail is hammered in, it is friction that holds it in place. ❷ Friction is the force that arises when two surfaces are sliding, or trying to slide, against each other. ❸ If you try to pull apart two blocks of wood that have been nailed together, the wood fibers grip the shaft of the nail. ❹ The nail feels a force trying to rip it apart along its length, and we call that force tension. ❺ Your experiment can now fail in one of two ways — either the nail stretches and splits in half because the tension force is too large for the nail, or the nail comes loose because the friction force is overcome. ❻ The force it would take to stretch the nail is much larger than the friction forces on the surface, so we don’t have to worry too much about the former. ❼ It’s the friction with which we need to concern ourselves.
choice.body: A hammered nail stays put because of friction, and although pulling joined blocks apart also creates (A)________ inside the nail, the nail is far more likely to (B)________ than to break, so friction is the factor that truly (C)________.

read.ko: 이런 일이 발생할 때, 몇몇 사람들은 여러분도 모르는 사이에 여러분의 하루에 아주 짧은 시간 조각을 추가하기로 결정한다.
read.en: When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge.

read.ko: 우리는 자연이 굴복할 것이라는 헛된 희망을 지니고 우리의 고정된, 인간이 만든 시간에 대한 관점을 자연에 강요하려고 노력한다.
read.en: We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield.

read.ko: 그러나 자연은 그러지 않는다.
read.en: It doesn’t.

para.en: When we realize we’ve said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands “know” what we’re going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech’s clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.

Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, “Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses.” This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.

Once a nail is hammered in, it is friction that holds it in place. Friction is the force that arises when two surfaces are sliding, or trying to slide, against each other. If you try to pull apart two blocks of wood that have been nailed together, the wood fibers grip the shaft of the nail. The nail feels a force trying to rip it apart along its length, and we call that force tension. Your experiment can now fail in one of two ways — either the nail stretches and splits in half because the tension force is too large for the nail, or the nail comes loose because the friction force is overcome. The force it would take to stretch the nail is much larger than the friction forces on the surface, so we don’t have to worry too much about the former. It’s the friction with which we need to concern ourselves.

There are numerous ways wildlife is managed, but they all imply stewardship and can be classified into two broad categories: active management and inactive management. Active management does something to the population — such as increasing or decreasing its size — in a direct manner through strategies like translocations or hunting, respectively. Populations can also be actively managed by altering the habitat to the benefit or disadvantage of a population. If population numbers are too low for the goal of management agencies, other active management can be incorporated, such as predator control to minimize neonatal deaths or habitat improvement to provide required cover for neonates from predators. These efforts represent active approaches to management. Other populations may not be actively managed, like those in national parks. In such situations, management activities minimize external influences on populations and habitat, which often involves management of humans and not animals.

Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone’s day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. For instance, when El Niño, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. Indeed, the Earth’s spin is generally slowing because the moon’s gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. Such events disturb the similarity between man-made time and more flexible time based on the Earth’s naturally occurring rotation. When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield. It doesn’t.

howto.word: 단락마다 밑줄 친 (번호) 중 어법·어휘상 틀린 것을 찾아요. 밑줄이 하나씩 나오면 O(맞음) 또는 X(틀림)를 누르고, X는 바로 아래 칸에 고쳐 씁니다. 어휘는 원문과 단어가 달라도 뜻이 같으면 O, 글의 흐름과 반대면 X예요. 틀린 부분만 써도 되고 밑줄 전체나 문장 전체로 고쳐 써도 됩니다(정답이 들어 있으면 정답). 밑줄을 모두 O·X 해야 다음 단락으로 넘어가요.
howto.cloze: 빈칸을 하나씩 보여 줘요. 우리말 뜻·유의어·첫 글자 힌트를 보고 원문 표현 그대로 쓰고 Enter(또는 다음 빈칸)를 누르세요. 빈칸을 모두 채워야 다음 지문으로 넘어가요.
howto.tf: 글과 일치하면 T, 아니면 F를 누르세요. 문장을 하나씩 보여 주고, 누르면 다음 문장으로 넘어가요. 지문은 아래 상자 안에서 스크롤하며 읽어요. 결과 화면에서 F 문장의 고칠 부분과 근거를 확인하세요.
howto.choice: 요약문 빈칸 · 추론할 수 없는 것 · 밑줄 의미를 고르는 5지선다예요. 지문은 상자 안에서 스크롤해요.
howto.order: 단락 (A)~(D)를 원래 글의 순서대로 눌러 주세요. 원문은 볼 수 없어요.
howto.insert: 주어진 문장이 들어갈 번호를 누르세요. 원문은 볼 수 없어요.

stems.word: 밑줄 친 부분이 맞으면 O, 어법·어휘상 틀린 것이면 X를 누르고 바르게 고치세요. (어휘는 뜻이 같으면 O)
